reviews.title: Horrible
reviews.text: This app is a horrible scam. There were barely any options within 60 miles of me. To add insult to injury, they have downright predatory subscription renewal practices. They offer you a huge sale for a 6-month membership and then automatically sign you up for a 12-month subscription at $86 split into 4 consecutive payments! I’m sure they know full well that the reminder email blends in with all of the spam they send you every day. If you purchase the subscription on their website, then you can’t use your phone to review and manage the subscription. It’s absolutely primative. I’m a single mother with $500 to my name and I just lost $176 because I didn’t know what was going on. Do not pay for this predatory service!

reviews.title: The app to make you feel like you alone are unmatchable.
reviews.text: High price. Zero results. Sure they parade a bunch of profiles before me and for weeks I’m reading them, liking, engaging. And getting zero returns. How is it I can engage with active users without them reaching out first but I can’t get even one like let alone a conversation even when I reach out first. Turns out the odds are not in most people’s favor on this app. Years ago it was a thriving active platform. Now it’s a ghost town except for a very niche group. So glad I wasted hundreds of dollars for nothing. Update your advertising for the people it works for and leave the rest of us alone. The modern dating scene is already demoralizing enough.

reviews.title: Awful service…. £350 and no access
reviews.text:
Having paid £350 for a premium subscription, nearly 3 days later I still don’t have premium access and cannot see any photos or respond to the likes I have received as eharmony have applied the premium benefits to an incorrect profile ID! Multiple
e-mails to their customer support team later and still no premium access and still £350 out of pocket!

reviews.title: Terrible platform
reviews.text: I didn’t receive any messages or leads. People seem to be lying about their age, too. I contacted customer support, and they told me my identity didn’t match public records, so my account had been blocked. On top of that, the algorithm wasn’t working properly with the answers I had provided. Overall, it was a pretty disappointing experience.

reviews.title: Scammer’s world
reviews.text: I got stuck with a year contract w/o reading fine prints. 80% of my Likes are scammers and their profile disappear in a week after matching(b/c they are using a week free trial account). After I appeal and complain to CS, “Likes” drastically increased suddenly but they’re still all scammers- somehow using Asian guys’ pictures from someone else’s Instagram(I think they’re paid ones). I appealed twice to cancel membership and got declined. I have no doubt that these 5-star reviews are paid ones. Do not get sucked for the membership- that’s how they maintain this app.

reviews.title: Ridiculous customer service
reviews.text: I had a guy like me, I went to like him back but my phone slipped and my finger hit the X instead. They absolutely refused to help me and kept giving me completely unrelated answers. It’s NOT THAT HARD to create an UNDO button or even for the customer rep able to undo the last unmatch. I’ve spent SO LONG on this app and finally got a decent guy that looked promising and they tell me that I should move on?!?

reviews.title: Expensive for no options
reviews.text: Do not purchase subscriptions to this site! Remember having a sub subscription does not necessarily mean they will send you any options for dating. The available profiles did not change in over two months, while I am still paying for a premium year membership I have deleted my profile and no longer use the site. Of all the dating apps I have used, this was the least helpful and showed the least options. Even though I no longer have a profile, they are still charging me per month for my yearly membership. Read the fine print y’all. They do not care whether you’re active or not. They do not care that there are no options for viable men or women to date. Mind you, I live in the New Orleans area. I have met people that are on eHarmony that I have dated, and their profiles never popped up, even though they fit within my filters. Buyer beware! Not worth the money, and you won’t be able to reach customer service regarding your concerns. They just take your money.

reviews.title: Misrepresentation of quality of product
reviews.text:
If you find that eharmony was deceptive in nature regarding your contract for membership and/or the product’s quality uwas misrepresented, you may want to double check your state’s consumer protection laws. If your state does not have a “cooling off period” law for internet contracts, you can still report the business to the attorney general. Additionally, states that have a “cooling off period” law in place for internet contracts got there by individuals writing their legislators and advocating for a statute change. eharmony functions the same as free apps with a disappointing personality quiz attached.

UPDATE: In response to the developer’s comment, I contacted customer care no less than a dozen times. They were unhelpful. If I could give zero stars, I would.

reviews.title: ⚠️‼️DO NOT PAY FOR THIS!!!‼️⚠️
reviews.text:
Ok so I got this app because the other apps I’ve been using just kind of seemed the same and figured eharmony you’d find more serious people, I was wrong! Like many have said, you run out of matches quick and you can’t see photos besides the few freebies you get when you sign up. The absolute worst part about this app is when you see it’s useless and want to cancel your subscription and close your account! Unlike other apps where you cancel a subscription and delete your account with ease this is the complete opposite!

Had the app for maybe a week and decided it was pointless and I wanted to cancel the subscription so I went through the process and it stated it was cancelled however 3 weeks later I got another charge! After finally finding the correct channel I sent a message to the customer support who would not issue a refund or close the account, all they did was read me a script about how eharmony is better than all the others and compatibility and blah blah blah! If this has happened to you and you’re locked into a subscription you can’t get out of then read on 👇🏻
After I found out they weren’t going to help and were going to keep charging for something I didn’t use or want I simply called my bank and filed a dispute which they also had the option to block all future charges which I opted in! Why complicate things when they don’t need to be complicated… makes no sense - just some constructive criticism. also cancel my account after seven days and had to pay compensation of £65. Why and for what exactly - Surely it should’ve been fair to say that I’ve used the subscription for one week out of my six months which would mean I should compensate you less than £5 - bit of a scam try match.com

reviews.title: eHarmony: Poison to Mental Health
reviews.text:
While cleaning up apps for space, I saw reviews that resonated with me so I wanted to share my experience even though it’s after the fact.

I deleted my eHarmony subscription after 1 year in August 2025 and leaving it unused since June 2025. I had high hopes in eHarmony because of the commercials I remembered as a preteen/teenager in the mid to late 2000s. Another friend married his lover through Facebook Dating so I had now-unfounded hopes that eHarmony would be a legitimate way to find love. Dating apps have historically been my only way to meet women because of not knowing where to develop connections in my current city outside work and life’s demands. Meeting possible dates in person seems risky anyway. I also need to focus on my career that was delayed by the pandemic and involved a switch to in-person work in a new city. I am in Texas where I am a Christian but I have poor relationships with most churches, making me uninterested in them. When I specified my faith as Christian, eHarmony mainly pulled up the fundamentalist, evangelical types I try to stay away from (also hurt my mental health in the past). But I am prone to people-pleasing so I changed my profile to appeal to this crowd early on. The platform was convincing early in its history but it has not changed with the times to improve match quality, expand its pool (especially for lonely/isolated people), or weed out scammers. reviews.title: Terrible App, Even Worse Cancellation Process
reviews.text:
My experience with eHarmony has been disappointing, to say the least. The app itself is underwhelming, but the cancellation process is where the real frustration begins.

Why does canceling a subscription require jumping through hoops, sending formal emails, providing account information, and practically writing an essay just to stop a company from taking your money? It makes absolutely no sense.

Signing up and taking my money was quick and effortless, but suddenly, when I want to cancel, it’s a complicated administrative process. If companies had to go through the same ridiculous procedures to collect payments from customers, they’d change their policies overnight.

I canceled my subscription approximately two months ago, yet I’m still being charged. Now I’m expected to go through additional steps to cancel something I already requested to cancel.

Here’s a revolutionary idea: If customers can subscribe with a few clicks, they should be able to cancel with a few clicks. No letters, no unnecessary emails, no obstacles, and certainly no begging a company to stop charging them.

eHarmony needs to seriously reconsider its customer service practices and subscription cancellation policies. Making it easy to take someone’s money but unnecessarily difficult to stop taking it is a terrible business practice.

I would not recommend this app. Save yourself the money, time, and frustration. Finding a compatible partner shouldn’t be easier than canceling a dating subscription.

reviews.title: I WANT MY MONEY BACK!!
reviews.text:
I WANT MY MONEY BACK!!

I’m stuck paying $200+ for a 3-month subscription, and I ran out of people to view on DAY ONE!

ALL profile photos are blurred unless you pay, so you’re basically forced to subscribe just to see who you’re actually considering. Then, once you’ve paid, there were barely any profiles within a 7-year age range, which is already a larger age gap than I want, and within the 30+ miles I’m already searching.

Then the app says to “Expand your search.” Meaning I have to increase the age range even more or search even farther away. For what?! 

And the worst part? You’re locked into the 3-month subscription and can’t cancel after realizing on DAY ONE that there’s no one to match with. They keep charging you for a service you’ve already exhausted.

Don’t waste your money. You’re better off on Hinge, CMB, Bumble, heck even Tinder. I wish I had spent my money on one of those instead, but instead I’m $200+ out, and no closer to meeting someone. 

I used eHarmony 2–3 years ago and had a completely different experience and was hopeful this time around too. 

Hundreds of dollars for what? I ran out of people on the first day. They clearly don’t spend the money to market towards the demographics they should (for reference, I’m 28).

reviews.text:

I am also extremely uncomfortable that even if I select my max distance to 30 miles, eharmony will continue to show my profile literally to people around the world. It’s creepy af.

Being forced to pay for 3 months at a time is also a gross subscription model. I can understand the intent behind it, but if I had known the privacy limitations, I would never have wasted my money.

The profile and questionnaire are fine, though, so a star each for that.

reviews.title: Poor Customer Service and No Goodwill
reviews.text:
My experience with eHarmony was disappointing—not because the service wasn’t a good fit for me, but because of how the company handled a very reasonable customer-service request.

I joined on July 19 and quickly realized that the platform wasn’t compatible with the way I approach dating. I contacted customer service to cancel and asked whether they would consider a partial refund given that I had used the service for less than a month. I explicitly acknowledged that my request was outside their stated cancellation policy. I was asking for a small gesture of goodwill—not disputing their terms.

Instead, I received multiple responses simply repeating a policy I already understood, followed by a patronizing offer to “spend time going over” concerns I had never raised and help I had never requested.

Even a $50 refund would have been a small gesture of good faith and could have left me with a positive impression of the company. Instead, eHarmony chose to rigidly hide behind its policy and then offered unsolicited “help” rather than actually addressing the request being made.

The result? They didn’t just lose a customer. They lost any goodwill that might have led me to recommend the company or consider it again in the future.

A company has every right to enforce its policies. But customer service is also about judgment, discretion, and knowing when a small gesture is worth more than rigidly enforcing the letter of a policy. eHarmony missed that opportunity completely.

There isn’t enough explanation about how everything works, and getting help or finding good customer service is difficult. I often found myself frustrated just trying to figure out how to use the service effectively.
What disappointed me most was how inactive and repetitive it felt. For months, I seemed to see the same profiles over and over again. I wish there were a better way to organize or set aside profiles you’ve already looked at so you can focus on new ones.
I took the time to complete my profile and genuinely tried to use the service, but after paying for an entire year, I didn’t get anything meaningful out of it—not even a conversation that went anywhere. The whole experience felt strangely empty.
Another thing I really disliked was the subscription policy. When you sign up, you agree to a long-term subscription with only a very short period to change your mind. After that, you’re basically committed to paying for the subscription even if you quickly realize the service isn’t what you expected. It left me with the impression that the policy is designed to lock customers in before they’ve had enough time to discover whether the service actually works for them.
I understand that no dating service can guarantee that you’ll meet someone, but for the price eHarmony

reviews.title: Fake Accounts and Fake Reviews
reviews.text: E-Harmony epitomizes fraud and dishonesty. Nearly all five-star reviews are fabrications; I've read them all, and most are just one-line comments lacking specific reasons for satisfaction. Additionally, 90% of their members are fake profiles, which explains why sending over 100 messages often results in no response. To inflate activity and create the illusion of a large community, they lure users into purchasing their outrageously expensive one-year annual membership for $495. They ask you to pay via their desktop website to avoid Apple fees. Once paid, they continuously charge the $495 annually unless you actively cancel—through both the app and the desktop site separately. They refuse refunds, prorated charges, or options for three-month plans. I intend to pursue legal action against their deceptive practices—faking member activity and misleading users into year-long commitments, then requiring separate cancellations on each platform. Victims should file complaints in small claims court or report their tactics online and to the Better Business Bureau to expose their dishonesty. They will likely respond with the same generic reply sent to hundreds of others. Even their so-called human representatives simply use automated responses, as fake as their fake profiles.

reviews.title: Scammers
reviews.text:
Avoid eHarmony at all costs. Their recurring billing is a deceptive scam — they lock you into automatic charges with barely any transparency, and canceling is intentionally difficult. I was charged again without clear warning, and customer support was useless. Don’t give them your credit card.
Refused a refund despite having sent an email when opening my account clearly stating that they did not have permission to bill my card without my express permission. I had to contact my bank and disputed the charges and got a refund from the bank. 
Companies that try to enforce the recurring billing as the default option usually do so for a reason - because customers wouldn’t resubscribe if they were given the choice.
Save your time and money and use Bumble, Hinge or Tinder - a fraction of the cost and far more people using them. The choice of people on eHarmony is limited due to the price… don’t be fooled into thinking you’ll see a different type of person, it’s just the same people that are on other dating apps that have given in to their curiosity and unjustified hype for an overpriced, underperforming app.

reviews.title: Don’t buy any membership and keep your money safe
reviews.text:
I purchased a two-year subscription last month and chose to split the payment into four installments of $117 each. About 45 days later, my account was frozen, and I was warned that if I don’t update my credit card information, I would lose access—and still be charged over $400.

I never requested to unsubscribe, and I explained that even though the platform is inactive and only a few people use it, I still want to keep my plan. Customer service said they canceled the automatic renewal for 2027, but I am still required to pay the remaining three installments. I told them I am willing to pay, but I need a clear statement showing the total amount, how much I’ve already paid, how much I owe, and the remaining balance.

Unfortunately, eHarmony’s customer service has been very poor. All I get are warnings, not real solutions. The platform feels outdated and poorly managed. I will consider filing a complaint with the BBB. Honestly, it’s not worth it, and I doubt anyone can find meaningful connections on this platform.

reviews.title: A classic dark-pattern subscription scam - avoid!
reviews.text:
I downloaded eHarmony on a friend’s recommendation, hoping to try something different from the usual dating apps. Unfortunately, the experience was deeply disappointing.

The app itself feels outdated and unintuitive, attempting to replicate platforms like Bumble or Hinge but without the same functionality or user base. Despite living in a major UK city, there were very few active users available, which immediately raised concerns about value for money.

What concerned me most, however, was discovering, only after signing up, that eHarmony locks users into a 12-month subscription, something that was not made sufficiently clear during the purchase process. After reading numerous similar reviews, I learned that many users have had issues cancelling within the 14-day cooling-off period, which is a statutory right under UK consumer law.

When I contacted customer support to cancel, I was told that because I had completed the personality questionnaire and briefly browsed profiles (I did not message anyone), I would be required to pay a £65 “value compensation” fee. In my view, this charge was not clearly or prominently explained at the point of purchase, nor does it feel proportionate to the limited use of the service.

Overall, the combination of a sparse user base, poor app experience, and unclear subscription practices makes this service hard to recommend. I would strongly advise prospective users to read the terms carefully and consider alternative platforms before signing up.
